> Automated review from Aiden's agent.
> 
>     * `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:127` classifies generic Bash `expansion` assignment values as safe to strip. That lets Bash 4.4+ prompt expansion hide executable work behind an allowlisted command. For example, `EVIL='$(touch /tmp/pwn)' FOO=${EVIL@P} echo hello` parses `FOO=${EVIL@P}` as an `expansion` with no `command_substitution` descendant, so this PR strips the env assignments and permission matching sees only `echo hello`. If the user has an allow rule like `echo *`, the command can be auto-approved while Bash executes the command substitution from the variable value during `${...@P}` expansion.

Ok, removed "expansion" and "arithmetic_expansion" from SAFE_ASSIGNMENT_VALUE_TYPES. It's hard to allow them and then try to filter malicious stuff out.

Additional clarification (regarding the scope of this bug)
This issue occurs specifically in the OpenCode Desktop (GUI) application, within the conversation‑panel built‑in shell. It does not affect the TUI (terminal user interface) version.

In the conversation panel, command output (stdout/stderr) containing Chinese characters is displayed as garbled text (� or mojibake), while the standalone terminal panel within the same application and the system’s native terminal both show the output correctly.

More importantly, we have confirmed that the output captured and sent to the AI context is also garbled – it is not just a front‑end rendering problem. This indicates that the stdout capture mechanism in the conversation‑panel shell already mishandles encoding (decoding UTF‑8 bytes using the wrong code page), causing corrupted data to be passed to the backend.

We kindly ask the development team to prioritise checking the encoding/decoding logic for stdout capture in the conversation shell, and to unify all terminal components to use UTF‑8 consistently.

@SMohsenM the MiMo V2.5 context limit is actually 1M tokens, and so it's an upstream issue.

Specifically, it's an issue with the `Output tokens` limit vs the `Context tokens` limit.

A second diagnostic utility here is that it stopped working without upgrading Opencode. So one day it worked, the next day not. I.e. upstream provider issue.

I dug fairly deeply through the codebase, and there is a way to actively bypass this, but the config change recommended in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/31152#issuecomment-4811330948 is the better short term approach.

However, I would suggest opencode show an error dialog in such cases as the passed JSON model config has some undefined values in this case, which could be caught, and then a human input box could be allowed.
